proof_summary: If the relevant Fermat number is prime, its totient equals the required power of two and the bound \(\varphi(m)<m\) proves minimality; if it is composite, \(\varphi(2^{N+1})=2^N\), and totient bounds force any smaller candidate to be odd with totient exactly \(2^N\). Every prime divisor of such an odd composite must be a distinct Fermat prime \(1+2^{2^a}\), so the totient factorization would express \(N=2^{33}\) as a sum of distinct powers \(2^a\) with \(a<33\), whose total is at most \(2^{33}-1\), a contradiction.
